Subject: Technical deep-dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs

Alex / Maya / Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. High-level notes below; I pulled these from the call and Aditya added technical context where helpful.

Pain points / goals (your stated priorities)
- Current inference 95th percentile latency spikes around peak traffic and during cold-starts — impacts user experience on search/ranking flows.
- Need consistent p95 latency target for short prompts (<= 64 tokens) of ~80ms across peak load.
- Throughput requirement: sustained ~300 requests/sec for classification/embedding endpoints; occasional bursts up to 600 rps.
- Model requirements: must support your custom fine-tuned model (3B-7B family), ~4k token context window, and be compatible with int8 quantized execution.
- Security/compliance: data encrypted at rest, SOC2 controls, and audit logs required for any production deployment.

What we propose (deployment options)
- Dedicated reserved capacity: recommend starting with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale headroom for bursts. This gives predictable throughput and low tail latency; we can map to your 300 rps sustained target with batching optimizations.
- Private (VPC) deployment: available if you prefer customer-managed network and on-prem-like isolation; same runtime and controls but with longer lead time for setup.
- Runtime optimizations we will apply: continuous batching tuned to your P99 sequence length distribution, KV/prefix caching for hot prompts, kernel selection favoring low-latency attention kernels, and warm pools to avoid cold start spikes.

Immediate asks / action items
- Marissa (me): sending SLO matrix and deployment proposal (attached) — please confirm whether p95 80ms and burst envelope look right.
- Alex: share a 48-hour representative traffic sample and an example payload distribution (short vs long prompts) — this will let us simulate batching behavior.
- Aditya: produce initial batch sizing and warm-up profile after we get traffic sample.

Attachments: nimbus_slo_matrix.xlsx, redwood-deployment-proposal.pdf (sent with this email)

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineering team — suggested times: Wed, Feb 24th 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu, Feb 25th 9:00–10:00 PT. Will include Aditya (runtime) and Camila (solutions).

If that all looks right, Alex please confirm the best time and share your 48-hour traffic dump (or a link) and any compliance contacts we should loop in.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks for the clear recap and for the proposal attachments. High level: that maps 1:1 with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- p95 80ms for <=64 tokens is the goal for our user-facing search API — agreed. For longer conversational contexts we can accept higher p95 (target 200–300ms).
- Traffic: I will share a 48-hour dump (anonymized) by EOD Monday. Format will be gzipped JSON with request timestamp, token counts, and endpoint.

- Stakeholders: Maya Patel (CTO) and Sarah Lee (Head of Security) will join the technical deep-dive.

Proposed time: Wed Feb 24th 10:00 PT works for our team. Please send calendar invite and dial-in.

Quick internal note —

Saw Alex's sample traffic; initial thoughts:
- For the 300 rps sustained target at p95 80ms for small prompts, we'll propose a continuous batching config with target batch sizes around 8–16 for the 3B class model (empirically low batch sizes minimize p95 while still getting good throughput).
- For bursts up to 600rps, propose a small cold pool of warm instances and faster autoscale policy (scale by GPU slots rather than whole machines).
- Kernel selection: prefer fused attention kernels plus int8-quant path; we'll include fallback paths for any model ops not supported by quantized kernels.

I'll produce a short benchmark and suggested batch/warmup parameters once I run the sample (will attach results).

Aditya
